history.summary: The accepted baseline mismatch at step 511 came from makemon.c:grow_up preserving sex in unsigned fem while JS passed Boolean false/true to pmname as an array index, selecting the neutral species name. The source-aligned fix now preserves integer 0/1 for name selection and comparison, then stores the sex bit as Boolean. The exact committed v54 replay at 9fa6482c0c9a58400f19f791d19bc39ce29c820f matches all 527 emitted screens, cursors, and RNG boundaries through step 526. It then stops at step 527 on the separate objnam.c:mshot_xname multishot missile ordinal refusal.

source.branch: When grow_up advances a monster into another species with neither M2_MALE nor M2_FEMALE, C preserves mtmp->female in unsigned fem and uses that 0/1 index in pmname; the JS fallback currently passes Boolean false/true as the array index and therefore selects the neutral name.
callers: muse.c:use_misc -> grow_up for MUSE_POT_GAIN_LEVEL; JS js/muse.js:use_misc -> js/makemon.js:grow_up. This selected session exercises the visible potion advancement path.
dependencies: do_name.c:pmname existing JS implementation in js/do_name.js

evidence: At makemon.c:2095-2117, C sets unsigned fem to 0 for M2_MALE, 1 for M2_FEMALE, or mtmp->female (an integer boolean); the evolution message formats pmname(ptr, fem) and compares fem to mtmp->female at 2141-2150. PM_ELVENKING in include/monsters.h:2679-2685 has neither male nor female flags and names [Elvenking, Elvenqueen, elven monarch].

At js/makemon.js:431-451 before the fix, the fallback assigned mtmp.female directly; Boolean false/true was not an array index in js/do_name.js:1239-1244, so pmname fell back to NEUTRAL. JS also used strict number-versus-boolean comparison for the verb. The fix in 9fa6482c0 converts the fallback and comparison to C-compatible numbers and stores Boolean(fem), preserving JS game-state shape.

The exact v54 session is unchanged (manifest cc258ba889b65b063f34199074d3313017b5d89ce3c175bb5443889ef9713e8e; recording b8b44533f0920ce54201cb4639f19ae5b6b56fb8ba3173161062128d28595f3c; recipe aa65292894c61d003af72136b11d3407c47b54a3bd7e1604fcf84dc027a2d557). source.branch: Compute xname(obj) first. If gm.m_shot.n > 1 and gm.m_shot.o equals obj->otyp, prepend "the <i><ordin(i)> "; otherwise return the ordinary xname unchanged.
callers: mthrowu.c:thitu uses mshot_xname(obj) for quantity-one incoming objects; JS js/mthrowu.js:thitu already calls it.

mthrowu.c:ohitmon passes mshot_xname to distant_name for visible hit/miss feedback from a monster missile; JS js/mthrowu.js:ohitmon passes the same callback. The selected run exercises the hit/miss message for an Elvenking arrow targeting the xan.

mthrowu.c:m_throw directly uses mshot_xname(singleobj) for visible sink-drop and missed-volley messages; JS js/mthrowu.js:m_throw evaluates the same name and sends both formatted lines through the existing message callback.
uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon_do_hit and hmon_hitmon_msg_hit use mshot_xname for thrown/kicked object feedback; JS js/uhitm.js has both calls.
dothrow.c:tmiss uses mshot_xname for player-thrown miss feedback; JS js/dothrow.js:tmiss already calls it.

evidence: objnam.c:1090-1102 is the complete function. It evaluates xname(obj) first; when gm.m_shot.n > 1 and gm.m_shot.o equals obj->otyp, it formats "the %d%s " from gm.m_shot.i and ordin(i), prepends it with strprepend, and returns the resulting name. Otherwise it returns the ordinary xname.

Required callees already have JS implementations: objnam.c:xname and strprepend in js/objnam.js, and hacklib.c:ordin in js/hacklib.js. The prefix branch preserves C evaluation order and uses the current volley index/type state. The sole UnsupportedObjectNameError throw class and its dead fail-closed registrations were removed.

The selected production path is mthrowu.c:m_throw -> ohitmon -> distant_name(otmp, mshot_xname) -> hit/miss, with JS js/mthrowu.js:m_throw -> ohitmon using the same callback. C mthrowu.c:ohitmon calls the callback for visible missile hit/miss lines; the admitted recording exercises the miss line against the xan. The separate m_throw flight-end sink/miss branches now evaluate The(mshot_xname(singleobj)) and send their source-formatted lines through env.message or ttyPline.

Other active direct C callsites are mthrowu.c:thitu, mthrowu.c:m_throw, uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon_do_hit/hmon_hitmon_msg_hit, and dothrow.c:tmiss. Their existing JS paths already call mshot_xname or pass it to distant_name.
